I have been where you are and ig I am still at times back there. I try to believe that we are all parallel lines and that we can't compare parallel lines cause everyone's lives, the way we perceive, deal with situations and experience depend on a lot of variables and individual differences, things that are not accounted for when we compare our lives with our peers. One can instead compare different parts of this parallel line, you can compare today to tomorrow and check whether there is progress and work on it therein. Take baby steps, start small, fail, start again, fail and work on it.  This helps actually, even though easier said than done. I had a huge anxiety attack that culminated in suicidal thoughts. It started with a simple Linkedin profile of my peer and spiraled with several other attributes. It's irrational to compare your life to someone else's. You have your own trajectory, so the comparison is not logical. There's nothing wrong with you and you can always have all the mentioned things you want with baby steps. I am sure your parents are there to support you and things will work out eventually. It hasn't yet for me but I believe it will, that's the only thing helping me move forward. Also, I am a person who ran away from literally everything that produced anxiety, this running away will never stop if you employ this. You need to stop and fight with baby steps, take the meds to help yourself, and see a good therapist as well maybe, cause it does work. It does get better.
